recentItems.title: Powerful bomb explodes at mosque near police offices in Pakistan, causing deaths and injuries
recentItems.description:
(18 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:


ASSOCIATED PRESS
Kohat, Pakistan - 18 September 2026
1. Wide of road near the mosque where a powerful bomb exploded, people gathered 
2. Mid of area nearby, people gathered
3. Red barriers near the road leading to the mosque area
4. Civil workers and others directing ambulance
5. Wide of people gathered at barriers
6. Ambulance 
7. People and emergency responders on road
8. Cars near road 
STORYLINE:
 A powerful bomb exploded Friday at a mosque near a building housing police offices in northwestern Pakistan, killing at least 15 people and wounding 56 others, police and rescue officials said. 

The attack came as violence has surged in the region with security forces targeting militants.

The bombing occurred in Kohat, a district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province bordering Afghanistan, when an attacker apparently rammed an explosives-laden vehicle into the mosque, said Zulfiqar Hameed, the provincial police chief.

Hospital officials have confirmed that five police officers and 10 civilians were among the dead, Bilal Faizi, a senior rescue official said. 

Most of those wounded were worshippers, he said. Some were in critical condition.

At least two armed gunmen also attempted to enter the police compound and exchanged fire with officers, police said.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the attack and expressed sorrow over the casualties. He directed authorities to accelerate rescue operations.

No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack, but suspicion was likely to fall on the Pakistani Taliban, formally known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP.

The attack comes a day after a roadside bomb struck a security forces convoy in the northwestern Hangu district and killed six soldiers. 

Government troops also conducted raids in various areas Thursday and killed 10 militants believed to be members of the Pakistani Taliban, the military and police said.

Pakistani Taliban have stepped up attacks on police and civilians in recent years. 

In 2023, a suicide bomber killed 101 people in an attack inside a mosque in Peshawar, the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

The group is separate from but allied with Afghanistan’s Taliban, which returned to power in 2021. 

Pakistan often accuses Kabul of sheltering the TTP and turning a blind eye to cross-border militant attacks. 

The government in Kabul has denied the allegations.

recentItems.title: New Interpol tool is uncovering hidden criminal assets: ONLY ON AP
recentItems.description:
(18 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Interpol Headquarters, Lyon, France - 17 September 2026
1. Tilt down of Interpol headquarters
2. Drone shot of Interpol headquarters lobby
3. Wide of Nicholas Court, Interpol director of task force coordination, walking in a corridor
4. SOUNDBITE (English) Nicholas Court, Director of task force coordination, Interpol:
"This is the first new Interpol notice for at least 20 years, and in really simple terms, it enables law enforcement officials who are looking for criminal money to send a message to the rest of the world that says: 'This person, this criminal, is worth this amount of money and we want to know where their assets are. We want to know if you, in other countries, can find their cars, their boats, their cash, their livestock, and can respond to us.' And then the countries, if they find money, can work together to make sure the money goes back to the country it should be in." 
5. Tilt up of Court in a glass elevator
6. SOUNDBITE (English) Nicholas Court, Director of task force coordination, Interpol:
"So, we introduced the new Silver Notice in January 2025 in a pilot. So, over the last 20 months or so, our countries have been using that to trace criminal assets from other parts of the world. They've been really successful. They have found at least €36 million worth of criminal assets in that time. There's plenty more time to go though. We anticipate that that will become a permanent capability of the organization. And over time, the hope is that that 36 million grows significantly and we start moving the needle and taking more of the money away from criminals by helping our countries to find out where they've stashed their illicit wealth."
7. Wide of Court walking
8. SOUNDBITE (English) Nicholas Court, Director of task force coordination, Interpol:
"The very first silver notice that was published, which was in January 2025, it related to a serious criminal based in Italy. The Italians knew that this criminal was worth a huge amount of money. But they also knew that most of his money was not in Italy. So they sent a silver notice to all Interpol member countries and within a few days, Brazil responded. And Brazil searched their databases and they were able to find numerous assets that were in the name of the criminal, in the name of associates of the criminal, related to property, to apartments, even to livestock. So, Brazil and Italy are now talking to each other in order to get the assets back from Brazil to Italy." 
9. Wide of Interpol logo on lobby floor
STORYLINE:
Interpol has rolled out a new tool to track down criminal assets hidden around the world.

The so-called "Silver Notice" allows member nations of the police cooperation organization based in Lyon, France, to notify and help each other when they're hunting for cash, cryptocurrency, cars, property and other illicit wealth stashed away by a suspected or convicted criminal that they have in custody. 

Nicholas Court, director of task force coordination at Interpol, said countries that have been testing the tool since last year have already proved its worth. 

"They've been really successful. They have found at least €36 million worth of criminal assets," he told The Associated Press in an interview at Interpol headquarters.

"Over time, the hope is that that 36 million grows significantly and we start moving the needle and taking more of the money away from criminals by helping our countries to find out where they've stashed their illicit wealth." 





AP Video and production by John Leicester

recentItems.title: A Palestinian family keeps traditional glassmaking alive, a craft passed down through generations
recentItems.description:
(18 Sep 2026) 
WEST BANK GLASSBLOWING

SOURCE: ASSOCIATED PRESS

RESTRICITON SUMMARY: 

LENGTH: 4:05

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Hebron, West Bank -  14 September 2026
1. Mid of Palestinian glassblower Yacoub al-Natsheh blowing glass 
2. Close up of al-Natsheh blowing into a metal pipe
3. Mid of glass being heated in a furnace
4. Wide of al-Natsheh crafting glassware, while surrounded by colorful glass ornaments
5. Mid of al-Natsheh crafting glassware
6. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Yacoub al-Natsheh, 64-year-old glassblower:
"I worked with my uncle for 49 years and learned from him. Then I began advancing my own skills. I tried to create something unique in Palestine, and I started inventing designs from my imagination and turning them into models, thank God. I am in this job for 59 years now, and we have maintained it within the al-Natsheh family."

7. Wide of worker break glass
8. Mid of shattered glass collected in a blue container
9. Various of glass melting process
10. Mid of glass being melted in a furnace
11. Wide of al-Natsheh crafting glassware surrounded by colorful glass ornaments
12. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Yacoub al-Natsheh, 64-year-old glassblower:
 “Our work is unique, no one can imitate it. I have watched a lot of manufacturers and glassblowers abroad, in Europe, where six or seven people work on a single piece. The one who blows doesn't know how to assemble, and the one who assembles doesn't know how to blow. Thank God, here we have work that no one can imitate. The same person crafts a piece from start to finish."

13. Al-Natsheh working with molten glass 
14. Al-Natsheh shaping molten glass 
15. Al-Natsheh crafting glass in workshop 
16. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Yacoub al-Natsheh, 64-year-old glassblower:
 "The tourism sector has been affected not by 50% but by 99%, due to October 7, the (Israel-Hamas) war, the situation, and people being exhausted. There is no tourism or visitors, even the visitors. Recently, the occupation has intensified restrictions in the (Hebron) old city, which have scared people away. People are afraid to come to the old city."

17. Wide of glassware and al-Natsheh
18. Mid of colorful vases
19. Wide of colorful glassware on shelves 
20. Mid of glassware 
21. Close up of colorful glass vases 
22. Wide of al-Natsheh glass workshop and factory 
23. SOUNDBITE (Arabic) Yacoub al-Natsheh, 64-year-old glassblower:
“In another ten years, God knows, it (craft) might disappear and become extinct because there are so few craftspeople left in the field. No one is willing to learn; it's a bit difficult, but with determination, you can achieve the impossible. I wish I could teach 20-30 people, for example, or students. What If they opened a section for glass education, in the (art) institute, or universities, I would be ready to teach."

24. Wide of al-Natsheh walking through a street in Hebron old city market 
25. Mid of al-Natsheh entering his glassware shop 
26. Close up of sign reading (Arabic/English): "The Factory of Canaan's Land for traditional handmade glass" 
27. Wide of Ibrahimi Mosque in Hebron
28. Wide of Hebron old city 
STORYLINE:
In front of his workshop's fiery kilns, Yacoub al-Natsheh blows through a long metal pipe, coaxing a glowing blob of molten glass into the shape of a vase. 

Glassmaking is a cultural staple in Hebron, the largest city in the occupied West Bank, where al-Natsheh says his family has practiced the craft for generations.

In Hebron’s Old City, he runs the last remaining traditional handmade-glass workshop.






“Our work is unique. No one can imitate it,” he added.

recentItems.title: China daily MOFA briefing highlights
recentItems.description:
(18 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Beijing, China -  18 September 2026
Spokesperson: Guo Jiakun

1. The Philippine Coast Guard says that this morning a China Coast Guard vessel rammed into a Philippine government vessel in waters off disputed Sabina Shoal in the South China Sea. What is the Foreign Ministry’s comment on this?

On the morning of the 18th, a Philippine government vessel made provocations and stirred up trouble in waters near Xianbin Reef (known as Sabina Shoal in English) in China’s Nansha Islands (Spratly Islands in English), deliberately ramming a China Coast Guard vessel, seriously endangering the safety of Chinese personnel and ships, and seriously violating international law and the basic norms of international relations. The Philippines should immediately stop its maritime infringements and provocations, stop spreading false narratives and stop confusing right and wrong. China will continue to firmly defend its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests, and firmly safeguard peace and stability in the South China Sea.

2. The EU is calling on the Chinese government to limit hybrid vehicle exports to Europe to no more than 15%. What is the Foreign Ministry’s comment?

For the specific question, I would refer you to the competent Chinese authorities. I would like to stress that the essence of China–EU economic and trade relations is mutual benefit and win-win, not zero-sum competition where one side loses and the other wins. Upholding open cooperation and resolving economic and trade differences through equal dialogue and consultation is in the common interests of both China and the EU. The development of China’s electric vehicle industry provides global consumers with high-quality, cost-effective products and makes a positive contribution to the global green and low‑carbon transition. We hope the EU will honor its commitments to market openness and free trade, abide by WTO rules, and provide a fair, just, and non‑discriminatory business environment for enterprises of all countries. We will closely monitor the EU’s actions and take necessary measures to safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese enterprises.

3. A US think tank report said that China has upgraded its military base at Djibouti and this upgrade significantly enhances China's ability to monitor military activity across the Middle East and Africa. Does the Foreign Ministry have a comment on this? 

I'm not aware of what you mentioned. I would like to reiterate that China has been the defender of world peace and a contributor to global development, and we will continue to play constructive roles in maintaining regional peace and stability on the principle of mutual benefit and equality. 

4. Commentary says that the security policies of the Takashi Sanae government show a dangerous trend of returning to the pre‑war era, and that Japanese society is being enveloped by an atmosphere that downplays the seriousness of war, and modern Japan is moving down a path reminiscent of the 1930s. Given that today is the 95th anniversary of the September 18th incident, does China have any comments on the recent dangerous moves by Japan in the military field? 


5. According to reports, China’s National Cultural Heritage Administration received two batches of cultural relics, artworks, and paleontological fossils, 64 items in total, returned by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security Investigations and the Manhattan District Attorney’s Office in Washington and New York this week. All were seized by U.S. law enforcement during their work. What is your comment?

recentItems.title: Ultra-Orthodox Jews prepare for Yom Kippur with Kaparot ritual
recentItems.description:
(18 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Jerusalem -  17 September 2026
1. Various of ultra-Orthodox men performing the Kaparot ritual 
2. Close of chickens 
3. Mid of a man performing the Kaparot ritual in front of a woman
4. SOUNDBITE (English) Shaya Rubin, Jerusalem resident: 
"We take the chickens and we put them around our heads, as we say the verse that this should be in our place, instead of us should be the chicken, meaning to say that we start the new year and we come to God, we come to Hashem asking for forgiveness. So we tell Hashem, we tell God, that this chicken should be in our stead."
5. Zoom of people praying next to the chicken distribution place
6. Chickens in a basket
7. SOUNDBITE (English) Shaya Rubin, Jerusalem resident:
"This tradition goes back already a thousand, hundreds of years, not a 1000 years. The sages tell us that it's one of the ways that we come to the Day of Atonement, Yom Kippur, with realizing our sins and asking for a kapparah, asking for forgiveness."
8. Mid of man taking a chicken out of the box
9. Mid of man handing chicken to ultra-Orthodox men performing the Kaparot ritual
10. Close of a book 
11. Various of a girl praying 
STORYLINE:
Ultra-Orthodox Jews prepared Thursday for the Jewish day of atonement, Yom Kippur, performed with the ritual of "Kaparot."

Observant Jews believe the ritual "Kaparot,” meaning atonements, transfers one’s sins from the past year into the chicken and is performed before the Day of Atonement, Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish year which begins at sundown on Sunday. 

One of the participants, Shaya Rubin, an ultra-Orthodox Jew from Jerusalem, said that he practices seeking forgiveness.

"We take the chickens and we put them around our heads, as we say the verse that this should be in our place, instead of us, should be the chicken," he said.

Israel’s ultra-Orthodox Jews, known as Haredim, make up around 14% of the country’s population. The insular community has long been at odds with the secular majority, clashing over military conscription, integration into the workforce and the basic tenets that guide their lives.

Israel’s Haredi population is also growing faster than any other group, at about 4% annually according to the Israel Democracy Institute’s 2025 Statistical Report on ultra-Orthodox society.

AP Video by Moshe Edri

recentItems.title: Polls open in Moscow for Russia's parliamentary election
recentItems.description:
(18 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

++PLEASE NOTE: AP IS OPERATING IN RUSSIA ACCORDING TO RUSSIAN RESTRICTIONS ON ALL REPORTING RELATED TO THE ONGOING MILITARY OPERATION IN UKRAINE++

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Moscow, Russia - 18 September 2026
1. Polling station workers getting ready, zoom out
2. Mid of observers
3. Wide of polling station interior
4. Close of voting machines
5. Various of woman being registered for voting
6. Pan of woman walking to the voting machine
7. Close up of woman at the voting machine
8. SOUNDBITE (Russian) Galina Vavilova, 82, Pensioner, Moscow resident:
"What do I expect (from the election)? Oh my God, improvement, an end to the war—that is the main thing, of course; that is the most important thing right now. Everyone wants peace, that’s what it comes down to. So that our guys are safe and sound."
9. Poster with information about candidates
10. SOUNDBITE (Russian) Lyudmila Kalinina, 79, Pensioner, Moscow resident:
"I would really like to see life stabilize for the better, meaning an end to the big divide between the ultra-rich and the extremely poor, because, after all, many people are living a very hard life."
11. Various of man receiving ballot papers and walking to the voting booth
12. Man casting ballot
13. SOUNDBITE (Russian) Vladimir Chubarev, 72, Professor, Moscow resident:
"As for the election expectations... The situation is certainly complex, so we wish for success—for all the important initiatives our government is undertaking to succeed. And, of course, for victory."
14. Man receiving ballot papers and walking to the voting booth
15. Man casting ballot
16. Close of ballot box
STORYLINE:
Polls opened in Moscow on Friday as Russia began three days of voting in the country’s  parliamentary election, which features virtually no opposition and is all but certain to secure the Kremlin’s political dominance.

Authorities spread the election out over the weekend in a bid to boost turnout among the 111 million eligible voters and even allowed electronic balloting. Polls opened across Russia’s 11 timezones on Friday and will end on Sunday.

Voters cast two separate ballots, filling half of the Duma’s 450 seats by selecting political parties listed on the ballot. The rest are contested in single-seat constituencies, with voters choosing individual candidates.

The main Kremlin party, United Russia, is all but assured to retain its overwhelming control of the lower house, the State Duma. Several smaller parties of the “systemic opposition” that vote in sync with the government on all key issues also are expected to retain their presence.

recentItems.title: Indonesia welcomes its first aircraft carrier, prompting debate over cost and military ambitions
recentItems.description:
(18 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Jakarta, Indonesia - 18 September 2026
1. Italian ship Giuseppe Garibaldi arriving at Jakarta port of Tanjung Priok
2. Members of Indonesian Navy on rubber boat and jet sky 
3. Tilt down Giuseppe Garibaldi
4. Various of marching band playing music welcoming Giuseppe Garibaldi
5. Giuseppe Garibaldi on docking process at port of Tanjung Priok 
6. Various of member of Italian Navy on board Giuseppe Garibaldi 
7. Italian ship Giuseppe Garibaldi docking at Tanjung Port of Jakarta
8. Chief of Indonesian Navy Adm. Muhammad Ali during press conference 
9. SOUNDBITE (Indonesian) Muhammad Ali, Chief of Indonesian Navy:
“We intend to use the ship primarily for military operations other than war, although it can also be deployed for combat missions if necessary." 
10. Giuseppe Garibaldi 
11. SOUNDBITE (Indonesian) Muhammad Ali, Chief of Indonesian Navy:
"We are a country that faces many natural disasters. We need a platform that can carry multiple helicopters so logistics and humanitarian assistance can be delivered quickly to affected and hard-to-reach regions,”
12. Various of Indonesian minister of Defense Sjafrie Sjamsoeddin (wearing brown shirt and black cap) being accompanied by Italian ambassador for Indonesia, Roberto Colaminè walking on board
13. Italian flag
14. Name of the ship written on the side of ship 
15. Pan right Italian ship docking at Jakarta port of Tanjung Priok
STORYLINE:
Indonesia welcomed its first aircraft carrier Friday, a former Italian warship that the government says will strengthen the archipelago nation's maritime security and disaster response capabilities.

The 41-year-old former ITS Giuseppe Garibaldi, with capacity for short takeoff and vertical landing aircraft and helicopters, was welcomed with a military ceremony upon its arrival at a naval base in North Jakarta’s Tanjung Priok seaport.

Italy in March agreed to give the carrier, which was retired in 2024, to Indonesia in a move aimed at boosting Italy’s broader defense engagement with the Southeast Asian country. Italy is seeking deals on submarines and aircraft, and gifting the carrier to Indonesia also saves the cost of decommissioning the ship.

“We intend to use the ship primarily for military operations other than war, although it can also be deployed for combat missions if necessary," Indonesian Navy chief Adm. Muhammad Ali told reporters after the ceremony. 

He said the carrier could serve the navy for another 15 to 20 years and could accommodate 14 helicopters or more, depending on their size.

Indonesia will become the second country in Southeast Asia with an aircraft carrier. Thailand’s HTMS Chakri Naruebet was commissioned in 1997 after being procured from Spain along with carrier-capable AV-8S Matador jump jets.

Ali said the carrier will be commissioned into the navy next week as the KRI Sriwijaya, honoring the Srivijaya empire, a maritime kingdom based in Sumatra that became one of Southeast Asia’s dominant naval and trading powers between the seventh and 13th centuries. Previously, the navy would name the carrier as KRI Gajah Mada.

Defense development was one of the top priorities for President Prabowo Subianto's administration, as he has advocated an expansion of the military through the purchase of submarines, frigates, fighter jets, and missiles and pushed for more defense cooperation with various countries.


Indonesia's Finance Ministry approved $450 million in financing for the aircraft carrier program in 2025.
